title: When the weather is frightful, you don’t need to be: everything we love to stay cozy during cold months
text:
When the weather starts to take a turn for the brisk, the impulse to stay inside and hibernate is nothing new – but there are ways to optimize your time spent inside for maximum coziness and pleasure.
From a limited-edition candle to a plush, furry comforter that does double duty, here are some of the ways our writers stay toasty even when the weather outside turns frightful.
Celestial Seasonings Tension Tamer Tea
I am deeply committed to a cozy lifestyle, and have piles of favorite soft blankets, warm socks and comfy pajamas around my home. But I also love having cozy rituals to round out my evenings, and one of them is having a nice cup of herbal tea. Tension Tamer, along with homemade chamomile and lavender blends, is a comforting classic and eases me into the end of the day gently. (It’s also perfect to pair with a book!) I love Tension Tamer because it is gently spiced and full of flavor without being overpowering, and it’s flavorful enough to stand in on those nights I kind of want a cocktail but don’t really want to drink. Julia Skinner
Celestial Seasonings Morning Thunder Tea
I have always preferred tea over coffee. While I appreciated the rich flavor of dark roast coffee, I sometimes found it too bitter. To get a decent cup from French roast beans requires grinding and pressing or an attentive slow pour. That is more effort than I want to expend first thing in the morning. That led me to explore roasted teas, starting with dandelion root, which comes surprisingly close to coffee. Still, something was missing. I wanted the deep round notes of coffee without losing the subtle flavor of tea. When I discovered roasted yerba mate, I knew I was close. My current favorite is Celestial Seasonings Morning Thunder, a blend of mate and black tea. It’s dark and smooth, with a satisfying roasted depth that doesn’t overpower the sweet, grassy notes I love in green mate. Morning Thunder has enough caffeine for a gentle lift without the intensity of coffee, and its warm, earthy aroma makes brewing a cup feel like a small daily ritual. Whether I’m starting a chilly morning or taking a midday break, it’s a cozy way to recharge. Alan Truly
Trudon Altaïr Candle
I have burned this newly released candle from Trudon weekly since getting my hands on it earlier this fall. It has an amazing throw (how far the candle’s scent travels) that somehow trickles into every room of my apartment without feeling overpowering, and I love how its woodsy scent leans more floral and delicate, without being too musky or earthy. When lit, the cedar notes are most noticeable, which makes it ideal for the holiday season. Oset Babür-Winter
Mornings at Levain x Snif Candle
The scent of something baking always makes a home feel a bit more welcoming. This candle collaboration between Levain Bakery and Snif is a fun alternative to having to whip up chocolate chip cookies for that same effect, with luxurious notes of vanilla, chocolate and even a bit of toasted walnut that really does smell like a morning at Levain Bakery. Lighting the candle and sipping a hot beverage while reading or having relaxing music playing certainly makes my evenings feel very snuggly and cozy – and bonus, I didn’t have to dirty a single dish to get that just-baked cookie aroma. Bernadette Machard de Gramont
Bedsure CloudBubble 2-in-1 Comforter Set
I got this comforter set for my son’s room, now that he is at university and the room will be used as a guest room for much of the year. The base of the set is a prewashed comforter that snaps on to a furry, sherpa-style blanket, so you have options: get cozy in the fabulous fluff or just use the comforter for the bed and the blanket for movie nights. Tobey Grumet Segal
Momcozy Nursing Pillow
In the three weeks since buying this nursing pillow, it has not left my lap. I use the crescent-shaped blob to support my son’s head and neck during feeds (and his hours-long contact naps that ensue), but you don’t have to be a breastfeeding parent to benefit: it serves as the ideal lap desk, allowing me to prop up my laptop or notebook while offering the ample elbow support that your typical lap desk doesn’t. Free of any rigid and harsh “corporate-friendly” materials such as wood, metal or plastic, you’ll find yourself hitting a flow state with unprecedented comfort. Luckily, this thing isn’t all business. It’s got a ledge designed to prop up your phone, should an endless scroll down TikTok lane sound like an appealing way to hibernate. Marissa Miller
Vankada Heating Pad
A few days each month, I help my wife, Tracey, at a small art gallery in Nova Scotia. Art2Sea’s brick building has an enormous display window and a drafty glass door, so chilly mornings used to mean bundling up and relying on hand warmers. Now I drape my Vankada heating pad over the office chair while opening up. By the time we’re finished, the seat is warm, and I drape the pad over my lap and sit comfortably without cranking up the space heater. The soft fabric immediately feels cozy, and the adjustable heat lets me dial in just the right warmth. The heating pad has six heat levels up to 140F and a safety timer that switches off in an hour or two. I start at the warmest setting but progressively lower the temperature as needed. It heats up again quickly whenever I want. There’s an energy-saving benefit as well. Running two 120W heating pads for six hours uses less electricity than running a typical 1,500W space heater for one hour. I love being comfortable without drying out the air or making the room stuffy for visitors. AT
Urbzue Hot Water Bottle with Cover
There’s nothing inviting about climbing into a cold bed on a frosty winter night. Even in autumn, that initial chill can be startling, and cold feet make it harder for me to settle down and fall asleep. A hot water bottle works but the bulging rectangular shape is surprisingly unfriendly. Fortunately, I found Urbzue’s long, narrow hot water bottle, which has a much more practical and comfortable design. Its slender shape and 29in length make it easy to tuck alongside a cold leg or cuddle against my torso without awkward corners digging into me. The soft, fuzzy cover adds another layer of comfort. I appreciate how something so inexpensive and simple can make bedtime feel luxurious. There is no cord to plug in, no controls to fiddle with, and no need to warm the whole room. I just fill it carefully with hot water, cap it and slip the warm tube under the covers to enjoy a cozy retreat from the cold until I wake in the morning. AT
Bearaby Heatable Weighted Lounger
I am generally warmer than I want to be in the colder months, thanks to the powerful steam heat that comes shrieking out of the radiators of my New York City apartment, but sometimes I want the best of both worlds: to be cozy on the sofa with the window ajar, blowing in a crisp, autumnal breeze. This sort of situation is only tolerable until, say, November. And when I really want to feel cozy, I turn to the Bearaby Lounger – a heated, weighted thing that’s really more comfortable to use than a full-on weighted blanket. Unlike traditional heated blankets, the Lounger requires no electricity. You just stuff it in the canvas bag it comes with, microwave it for a minute and drape it over whatever part of your body needs it. It’s filled with something called Terraclay – which the brand says has heat-retaining qualities – and the weight itself is gentle at just 6lbs, so it’s perfect for beginners. Megan Reynolds
Saxx Snooze Pajamas
I think getting older makes you care more about looking and feeling like an adult. Take sleepwear: I didn’t start setting aside clothes just for bed until well after college. Gym clothes had always seemed fine to sleep in, but purpose-made sleepwear feels even better. I don’t mean goofy holiday pajamas. I mean pants and a shirt so comfy you look forward to bedtime. This matching set is made from modal, a fabric derived from beech trees. It drapes beautifully and feels so smooth it makes cotton seem rough by comparison. It’s also breathable and wicks away sweat at night. Thoughtful details abound, including flat seams to reduce chafing, hand pockets, and a drawstring that won’t disappear into the waistband – and in the end, this is what makes them feel like the equivalent of Sunday morning pancakes. Sal Vaglica
Soundcore A20 Sleep Earbuds
Earbuds designed for sleep have become a category of their own, and I have tested plenty. Still, I keep coming back to the Soundcore A20s – even after the company released a newer version. They’re small, with grippy silicone that keeps them in place through a night of tossing and turning, and they’re comfortable enough that you barely notice them. Side sleepers may want to try a pillow with an ear-shaped cutout to keep pressure off the earbuds. The A20s also have an intuitive app with customizable white noise. I start the night with a boring ESPN baseball podcast, then let the earbuds switch to my soothing mix of a washing machine, traffic and rain on a tent. SV
Kitsch Weighted Satin Eye Mask 
This eye mask ticks all the boxes I have for finding the perfect eye mask. Not only does the soft satin exterior feel comfortable next to my skin, but it offers a secure strap to keep it in place all night and comes weighted with subtly scented lavender microbeads to help me fall asleep. JS
Ugg Scuffette II Slippers
It may be a cliche choice, but when it’s chilly, I turn to my Uggs to keep my toes warm. These sheepskin-lined slippers do the trick and slip on and off easily – no hands required. I especially love them for walking the dog, or for heading to yoga since sneakers can be a pain to deal with. The rounded toe gives your feet room to spread out, and the suede exterior is fairly easy to keep clean with light brushing every so often. The soles are good for indoor and light outdoor use, so I wouldn’t wear them for heavy walking days, but I do like them for running quick errands in the car. If the classic chestnut colorway isn’t your jam, you can pick from a handful of other color options, including black. BMDG
Glerups Slip-on Leather Slippers
Fluffy slippers lined with lofted fleece or shearling seem cozy – until you flatten the insoles into oblivion or stink up the insides. Enter Glerups. Made from breathable 100% wool that is felted into these nearly indestructible flexible leather soles, the unisex slippers come in 16 colors and two additional heights. (And if you plan to wear them for coffee runs or trips to the mailbox, you can opt for a rubber sole instead of leather.) After six years, mine recently developed a small hole where my big toe rubs against the felt. I was about to replace them with a new pair when I discovered that the company will send a felt patch free of charge. Here’s hoping an easy repair keeps them in my closet and out of the landfill for many more years to come. JD
Bombas Gripper Slippers
After many visits struggling with the cold stone floors at my in-laws’ 16th-century countryside home in south-west France (a niche problem, I know), I discovered the Bombas Gripper Slipper. Built like a soft bootie, these are made of a thick blend of merino wool and nylon, and have grips on the bottom so you can easily walk on hardwood and tile flooring without sliding. The footbed is padded, so you get a little more support than you would from wearing just socks. They are very effective at keeping my feet warm, and they have their own storage bag that you can pack them in, making them perfect for travel. BMDG
Poplight Wireless Wall Sconce
I’m no Kelly Wearstler, but I know a thing or two about lighting choices that make a space feel inviting. First stop: I have foregone use of my godawful overhead pot lights in favor of these charming and rechargeable Shark Tank-famous wall sconces. I especially appreciate that they’re renter-friendly and suitable for the commitment-averse, as they stick on in seconds, leaving no damage behind. They impart a range of comforting (and flattering!) light settings, whether you need real visibility to read or an ambient glow to set a vibe (it is cuffing season, after all). MM
Nautilus Vintage Ski Posters Wooden Jigsaw Puzzle
There’s always a puzzle in progress at my house, pieces strewn all over the coffee table. It’s the ultimate cozy activity during evenings at home, often with a comfort movie playing in the background. This high-quality wooden jigsaw puzzle is one of my favorites – the nostalgic artwork and “whimsy” ski shapes of each piece make it a joy to put together, and a few posters evoke fond memories of visits to those destinations. Paige Triola
Amazon Kindle Paperwhite
Nothing makes me happier than snuggling up with a good novel, and I have been a steadfast Kindle user since 2008, when I used to read while I nursed my son (and could use one hand to turn the pages). As a Brooklyn apartment dweller, ebooks are the perfect alternative to the real thing because I only have so many bookshelves I can fill. The newest iteration of the Kindle Paperwhite is bigger and brighter than the previous version, and still comes with an IPXG waterproof rating – so I can even take it for a long soak in a hot tub. Plus, its screen is now totally flush, which makes it a little more comfy to hold. TGS
Wellfleet Oyster Festival Sweatshirt
Sweatshirts are an incredibly personal item of clothing because what makes a good one is different for everybody. As a particularly picky individual, I have a lot of inside-the-house sweatshirts that are just about perfect, except for one little thing – but this guy, bought at the Wellfleet Oyster festival a decade ago, is ideal. The sweatshirt itself is from Comfort Colors, printed with the Wellfleet Oyster festival’s logo, and was perfectly smooth, soft and broken-in from the jump – and has only gotten better with age. It’s the right weight for layering under whatever strange assemblage of outwear required for late fall’s hot, then cold, weather. Nothing in life is perfect, but this comes close enough for me! MR
Buck Mason Shrunken Graduate Blazer
Ladies and gentlemen, I give you the most comfortable blazer I’ve ever worn. Like a cozy blanket I can wrap around my shoulders, the blazer is crafted from soft shetland tweed with a snug, vintage fit. Form and function in the best ways possible: it keeps me warm on chilly days, it’s perfect for work or play, and it’s my favorite travel companion for the plane and beyond. TGS
&Daughter Glenn V-Neck Sweater
When it comes to cozy knits, &Daughter is the brand I save up for. Each piece is a bit of an investment, but I wear mine often enough that the cost-per-wear comes out to be a much better decision than spending, say, $250 on a sweater with acrylic or polyblend. This gorgeous V-neck has a plush, five-gauge knit (100% wool, obviously) that somehow feels incredibly lightweight and warm; I’ve yet to find another sweater that does both so well. I also love layering different colors of tees underneath, from a pop of red to classic white. OBW
Patagonia Down Sweater Hoody
This lightweight jacket has gotten me through 11 winters and counting in rainy Portland, Oregon. When it’s wet and cold outside, I layer it over a sweater and under a rain shell. And on dry days when the temps are in the 40s and 50s, it’s warm enough to wear on its own. The ripstop outer is windproof and water-repellent, while 800-fill-power goose down gives it a high warmth-to-weight ratio. Use the adjustable cords at the hood and hem to seal in warmth and the internal zippered chest pocket as a stuff sack for travel. One of my favorite features? The velvety “zipper garage” at the top, which keeps the jacket from rubbing against your chin when it’s zipped all the way up. JD
The Landmark Project Haven Full Snap Sherpa Jacket
The warmth and roomy fit of this fleece make it a great choice for chilly weather – but it’s the soft natural hues, charming floral pattern, and corduroy collar and pockets that make it my go-to for pumpkin picking or lounging by the campfire. For me, it perfectly captures the feeling of being at home in nature. (There is also a half-snap, unisex sherpa jacket available, so everyone can be cozy outside.) PT
Lands’ End Insulated Diamond Quilted Maxi Coat
Last year, winter finally got to me. I couldn’t take being cold any more. To hell with flattering coats, I went full sleeping-bag, puffer-to-the-boot-tops with this coat from Lands’ End, in the down-free option since I don’t like feathers for allergy- and Peta-related reasons. It’s water resistant and made with recycled fabrics and insulation (17 recycled bottles’ worth per coat). The two-way zipper is comfortable when I have to sit in the car for a while or when I get warm while hiking with the dogs. The big patch pockets on the hips are great for jamming mittens or holding a phone for a few minutes – and there’s a more secure zip pocket inside the chest. The coat is rated for -13 to 18F temperatures and keeps me toasty. Maria Ricapito
Lululemon Wunder Puff Cropped Vest
We’re in that in-between weather where I can’t quite commit to a full puffer jacket, but I require an added layer of insulation to keep me warm on my daily 20,000-step stroller walks. The Lululemon Wunder Puff vest never fails to guard me against the elements while giving me room to breathe. Its generous pockets allow me to tote an obscene amount of stuff, and its detachable hood extends just enough to keep rain and debris out of my eyes. A cinchable hem further keeps wind at bay while accentuating my waist. Oversized baffles stuffed with 600-fill-power goose down keep me toasty wherever I go. Mostly, though, it elevates any outfit, conveniently concealing the parts of my shirt most frequently covered in spit-up. MM
